Theme

Money, work & business

accounts noun

a record of money received and paid

also account, account books, keep accounts, keep books, bookkeeping, accounting, audit accounts, balance the accounts, the account balances, the books, keep the books

classical

Cic. Att. 5.21.12: ratiōnēs cōnferātis (Lewis & Short s.v. conveniō)
Traupman 163
Cic. Att. 4.11.1: ratiōnēs cum pūblicānīs putāre (Lewis & Short s.v. ratiō)
Traupman 268

ratiōnēs, ratiōnum f. pl.

plural of ratiō, ratiōnis f. · Declension on Wiktionary

accounts, reckonings

A single account is ratiō; ratiō cōnstat, “the account agrees”, is the merchants’ phrase for books that balance.

Other words

  • tabulae, tabulārum f. pl. — account books, the books

    noun, first declension, plural · also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 2.97: tabulās cōnficere, to keep books (Lewis & Short s.v. tabula); Traupman 163; Cic. Verr. 2.1.60: tabulās cōnficere (Lewis & Short s.v. tabula); Traupman 268 · Declension on Wiktionary

    In full tabulae acceptī et expēnsī, the books of receipts and payments.

  • dispungō, dispungere, dispūnxī, dispūnctum — audit, check off (an account)

    verb, third conjugation · also used · post-classical · Dig. 50.16.56 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 163; Sen. Ben. 4.32: ratiōnēs expēnsōrum et acceptōrum (Lewis & Short); Traupman 268 · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    A term of post-Augustan business Latin (Lewis & Short).
